beats.text: In the late 1970s, geophysicists Glen Penfield and Antonio Camargo were mapping the Gulf of Mexico.
beats.say: In the late 1970s, geophysicists Glen Penfield and Antonio Camargo were mapping the Gulf of Mexico.

beats.text: They noticed a circular anomaly, a possible impact crater buried under the Yucatán Peninsula.
beats.say: They noticed a circular anomaly, a possible impact crater buried under the Yucatán Peninsula.

beats.text: In 1991, Penfield and Alan Hildebrand confirmed it was the Chicxulub crater, linked to the K–Pg extinction.
beats.say: In 1991, Penfield and Alan Hildebrand confirmed it was the Chicxulub crater, linked to the K–Pg extinction.

beats.text: Estimated 66 million years old, it’s one of Earth’s largest impact craters, alongside the much older Sudbury and Vredefort impact structures.
beats.say: Estimated 66 million years old, it’s one of Earth’s largest impact craters, alongside the much older Sudbury and Vredefort impact structures.

beats.text: The impact site was a marine carbonate platform, 650 meters deep at its center, with water depths varying from 100 meters on the western edge to over 1,200 meters on the northeastern edge.
beats.say: The impact site was a marine carbonate platform, 650 meters deep at its center, with water depths varying from 100 meters on the western edge to over 1,200 meters on the northeastern edge.

beats.text: Today, the crater is 300 kilometers wide, with a buried peak ring, making it one of the largest impact structures on Earth.

facts.claim: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater buried underneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico.
facts.quote: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater buried underneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico.

facts.claim: The crater is estimated to be 200 kilometers in diameter and is buried to a depth of about one kilometer beneath younger sedimentary rocks.
facts.quote: It was formed slightly over 66 million years ago when an asteroid, about ten kilometers in diameter, struck Earth. The crater is estimated to be two hundred kilometers (120 mi) in diameter and is buried to a depth of about one kilometer (0.6 mi) beneath younger sedimentary rocks.

facts.claim: The impact site was a marine carbonate platform, 650 meters deep at its center.
facts.quote: The water depth at the impact site varied from 100 meters (330 ft) on the western edge of the crater to over 1,200 meters (3,900 ft) on the northeastern edge, with an estimated depth at the center of the impact of approximately 650 meters (2,130 ft).

facts.claim: The crater is one of the largest impact structures on Earth, alongside the much older Sudbury and Vredefort impact structures.
facts.quote: It is one of the largest impact structures on Earth, alongside the much older Sudbury and Vredefort impact structures, and the only one whose peak ring is intact and directly accessible for scientific research.
